clue.text: Not be happy with fool for breaking joint

indicators.note: breaking signals that the pieces force their way into the middle of the joint word

parts.note: a dive is a seedy joint, a low bar or club
a sap is a gullible fool
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Someone is unhappy that a clown has broken into a seedy bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' is the container signal: the fool and the 'for' word split the joint open.
explanation.definitionFit: To disapprove of something is to frown on it, to not be happy with it.

clue.text: Take off, and land

definitions.meaning: to take money off someone's pay is to deduct it
to bring a ship or spacecraft in to berth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' and 'land' look like a flight's two ends, but each is a separate definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Docking wages deducts from them; a ship or spacecraft docks when it berths or arrives.

clue.text: Wheel hurries up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: nips means hurries, as in nipping out to the shops

explanation.definitionFit: To wheel is to turn round quickly, to whirl or rotate.

clue.text: Hear Greek character has billion to pay

parts.note: to pick up a sound or signal is to hear it
theta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek figure owes a billion and must settle up.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up the bill or the tab is an idiom for paying for everyone.

clue.text: Sorry for bankruptcy, heading for gutter

parts.note: ruin is financial collapse, bankruptcy

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of the following word, its head

explanation.surface: Someone regrets the bankruptcy that sent them into the gutter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruing something means regretting it, feeling sorry for it.

clue.text: The Spanish check inside even knitted fabric

indicators.note: inside places the first pieces within the rearranged word
knitted suggests the letters are worked together into a new pattern

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
to vet is to check thoroughly

explanation.surface: A Spaniard inspects an evenly knitted cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knitted' makes VEEN, and 'inside' is the container signal for the Spanish article and the check.
explanation.definitionFit: Velveteen is a cotton fabric with a pile imitating velvet.

clue.text: Report — one the police sent over

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: sent over means turned over, read back to front

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: A news report about someone the police have dispatched.
explanation.walkthrough: THE MET is London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single report or piece of news in a paper or bulletin.

clue.text: Why one's unable to take down in rows such kitchen equipment

indicators.note: in places the reason phrase inside the word for rows

parts.note: tiers are rows set one above another

parts.words: Why one's unable to take down
parts.note: a person cannot write anything down because they have no pen

explanation.surface: A puzzled cook asks why they can't fetch the gadgets stacked on shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'such' is a link. Having no pen is why one cannot take notes down.
explanation.definitionFit: Tin-openers are kitchen gadgets for cutting the lids off cans.

clue.text: Fashion sound underwear, to cover upper-class lord's seat

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for fashion is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: manner means fashion, way of doing something

indicators.note: to cover means the underwear word wraps around the letter

parts.note: hose are stockings or tights, worn under clothes

explanation.surface: A designer of underwear works to suit a lord's country home.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor house is the main residence of a lord of the manor, his seat.

clue.text: Feature film that's frightening, say, little furry animal

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature

indicators.note: say signals the word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a chiller is a frightening film

explanation.surface: A creature feature with a cute furry star.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinchilla is a small South American rodent with very soft fur.

clue.text: Thus initialled author with no name?

definitions.text: Thus initialled author with no name?

parts.words: Thus initialled author with no name?
parts.note: an unknown writer has no name to sign, so a clipped form of the word for nameless stands in for one

explanation.definitionFit: Anon, short for anonymous, is printed in place of the name of an unknown author.

clue.text: How does a lollipop pass quality control?

definitions.text: How does a lollipop pass quality control?

parts.words: How does a lollipop pass quality control?
parts.note: a sweet is tested by licking it, and the phrase also means try something to find out whether it works

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means try something out and see what happens, here applied to sucking a sweet.

clue.text: For whom spring rapidly follows fall

definitions.text: For whom spring rapidly follows fall

parts.words: For whom spring rapidly follows fall
parts.note: spring is a bounce and fall a drop, not seasons; this daredevil drops from a height and rebounds on an elastic cord

explanation.definitionFit: Such a jumper leaps from a height tied to an elastic cord, plunging and then springing back up.

clue.text: Break monster flower

parts.note: to snap is to break
a dragon is a mythical monster

explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon is a garden plant whose flowers open like a mouth.

clue.text: Act of hostility takes years to install King George over Jewish people

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first part sits above the second
to install means to set the king inside the word for years

parts.note: ages means a long time, years
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
Sion, or Zion, is used for the Jewish people

explanation.surface: Installing King George over the Jewish people takes years and is a hostile act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to install' is the container signal and 'over' stacks the pieces in this down clue; 'takes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggression is hostile behaviour, an unprovoked attack.

clue.text: Awful thing approaching foreign waters results in hellish event

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Awful thing approaching foreign waters results in hellish event' gives NIGH (approaching) and MARE (foreign waters) but nothing for the T; the clue seems garbled and no source gives the original.
annotationWithheld.clue: Awful thing approaching foreign waters results in hellish event

clue.text: Animal is a right rabid, dicky duck!

parts.note: rabid means mad
dicky is British slang for unwell, ill
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a mad, sick duck.
explanation.walkthrough: DICKY is British slang for feeble or unwell, as in a dicky heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is a South American mammal with a bony armoured shell.

clue.text: Combat's purpose seen in conclusive victory

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: seen in means one word appears inside the other

parts.note: a KO, or knockout, is a decisive win
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: The point of fighting is to be seen winning outright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' is the container signal; KO, a knockout, is the boxing term.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendo is a Japanese martial art of combat with bamboo swords.

clue.text: Empty gallons, needing sterile packaging

indicators.note: packaging means the sterile word wraps around the letter

parts.note: pure means clean, sterile

explanation.surface: Gallons of liquid are drained into germ-free containers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'packaging' puts G inside PURE; 'needing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To purge is to empty out or clear something completely.

clue.text: Backing a war, terribly smart for old soldier

indicators.note: backing means the words are read in reverse

parts.note: Nam is short for the Vietnam War

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A veteran is pained by a war he once supported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' turns A NAM into MANA; 'terribly' rearranges SMART into TARMS.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-at-arms was a medieval armed soldier, especially a mounted one.

clue.text: Get up slope in Andes, struggling to maintain height

parts.note: a rise is an upward slope

indicators.note: to maintain means the rearranged letters hold the letter inside
struggling signals the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A climber struggles up a slope in the Andes, trying to keep altitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' makes ANDSINE, and 'to maintain' is the container signal holding the height letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rise and shine is a cheerful order to get up out of bed.

clue.text: Author standing the test of time?

explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy wrote Tess of the d'Urbervilles; hardy means robust and able to endure.

clue.text: Opponent taking a pole and twisting it books fi

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Opponent taking a pole and twisting it books fi' ends in stray words 'books fi' that give nothing; A + N + reversed IT fits the rest, but the printed clue cannot be confirmed.

clue.text: You shouldn't trust me as a hero!

definitions.text: You shouldn't trust me as a hero!

parts.words: You shouldn't trust me as a hero!
parts.note: the speaker admits to being a swindler who cheats people, yet is an idol

explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a revered figure or hero; split in two it reads as a confession of cheating.

clue.text: Good to deliver this structure?

parts.note: to rid is to free or deliver from something

explanation.surface: A request to build the framework that the solver is filling in.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid is a network of crossing lines, the framework of a crossword.

clue.text: Too high to catch?

parts.note: high means high-pitched, and catch means hear, not seize

explanation.definitionFit: Ultrasonic sound is pitched above the range of human hearing.

clue.text: Not entirely ten need just this?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Not entirely ten need just this?' gives no parse for the answer; it looks garbled and no source gives the original.
annotationWithheld.clue: Not entirely ten need just this?

clue.text: Surprisingly, Nepal noisy in relation to Hawaii

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the letters land in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Nepal turns out unexpectedly loud compared with Hawaii.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawaii lies in Polynesia, the Pacific island group, so things relating to it are Polynesian.
